data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 3-of-26 result is not evidence about when tests constrain versus describe; it is an artifact of mutation proposal order and guard installation order in one repository, and the distribution (compile.py 1/9 vs. 4/4 to 6/7) reflects the arbitrary order in which shown-to-fail-first guards were installed by the author, not any generalizable condition.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the mutation proposal and guard installation order were randomized across the project, the distribution would not show the observed asymmetry.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py mutations were all evaluated before any guard installation while other modules were evaluated after, the order effect would be trivial but the 3-of-26 result would not generalize.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the same distribution replicated with a different author following a different order, the order-effect explanation would weaken.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a formal policy mandated guard-before-mutation ordering and compile.py still showed 1/9, the arbitrariness claim would fail.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Mutation proposals and guard installations are sequential in a single-author workflow. A mutation is lost only if a shown-to-fail-first guard for its code path has already been installed when the mutation is evaluated. In compile.py, the guard installation order left only one of nine mutations covered at evaluation time; in the ordinarily-guarded modules, the author installed guards before proposing mutations, so most or all mutations were covered. The apparent 'condition' is an order effect: the test constrains the subject when the guard installation precedes the mutation proposal, and this precedence is arbitrary and unmeasured.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
